scope: Complete modern single-jib crane interpretation of Ms B49r. A human drives and holds a single-part hoist. Slewing stays locked during the lift. Counterweight, support details, dimensions and loads are modern choices. The optional ratchet is visible with its pawl parked clear.

folio.holder: Bibliothèque de l Institut de France

date.note: Approximate manuscript dating, not a dated completion record.

folio.verification_note: Edition foliation and text verified through e-Leo. Original-holder service may be unavailable. e-Leo viewer is an authorised-edition resource, not the original holding institution.

scale_m.note: Full swept bound. All chosen dimensions are modern explanatory assumptions, never claimed measurements of a historical machine. Measured at rest: the base spans x and z [-1.0, 1.0], the load's far face reaches z=1.70 and the jib's beams y=2.79 over a base whose underside is y=-0.05; slewed, the upper works sweep a radius of at most 1.703 m.

frame.transforms: All part positions relative to their named parent. Joint q is an extra rotation or translation about the declared parent-frame pivot applied to the rest transform. Children inherit it once.

assumptions.statement: Every numerical part size, position, orientation and support arrangement in parts is a declared modern modelling choice unless a separate primary source is explicitly attached. Materials marked assumed are plausible period choices. They are not measured from any museum replica.
assumptions.reason: Leonardo did not provide a manufacturing drawing with all dimensions.

assumptions.statement: The stated rates and loads are slow modern demonstration choices. They do not reproduce a measured speed in Leonardo s workshop.
assumptions.reason: No historical operating record was located.

assumptions.statement: The mast is offset to z=-0.20 m to clear the drum and rear rope. Explicit bored journals, pulley cheeks, axles, crossbar, bracket and exterior crank complete this modern structural interpretation. The optional 24-tooth ratchet is inactive and the human must hold the final load.
assumptions.reason: Complete the numerical modern demonstration without presenting invented details as Leonardo dimensions.

At each frame regenerate 65 points with theta_i=(1-q_hoist)*i/64 for i=0..64, centreline=(-0.08*sin(theta_i-1),0,-0.08*cos(theta_i-1)). Parent drum rotation is applied exactly once. At q_hoist=0 the wrap angle is 1 rad. At q_hoist=-3 it is 4 rad. Its free end stays at drum-world offset (0,0,-0.08), tangent to the upward exposed strand. Winding remains below one full turn, so the rope never overlaps itself. The attached end remains fixed to the drum.

At phase t replace final centreline point y by 0.82+0.02*t. Other exposed points stay fixed. Exposed length falls by 0.02*t and the drum-wrap length rises by exactly the same amount. The initial exposed path length is 4.68+pi*0.08 m. Initial drum-wrap length is 0.08 m. The total rope length is 4.76+pi*0.08=5.011327412287183 m. The pulley pitch radius and drum rope centreline radius are 0.08 m. Both solid radii are 0.075 m, tangent to the rope radius 0.005 m.

joints.notes: The platform now stands on a ring of rollers; its frame is 0.08 m higher.

q_lift=-0.08*q_hoist. q_rear=q_tip=q_hoist. All three axial rotations are negative about +X during lifting. Single supporting strand. The exactly specified drum-wrap supplies the changing exposed length.

input_rate.note: A human turns hoist at2.39rpm. A modern assumed holding pawl carries the stopped load.

drive.justification: A human turns hoist at2.39rpm. A modern assumed holding pawl carries the stopped load. The positive input rate is a speed magnitude. The input joint hoist turns negatively about +X.

motion.final_hold: At 12 s the human continues to hold the handle with ideal 39.2 N tangential force. The pawl remains visibly disengaged. There is no automatic arrest, lowering or rearming cycle.
motion.visitor_12s: Load rises0.24m. The platform stays locked. No swinging.

animation_notes: No bounce, no hidden energy recharge and no invisible reset.
All independent joints are in the schedule. Rigid descendants follow their parent.
Use the specified SI time without cinematic speed-up.

Keep the optional pawl parked at its specified rest position, clear of the ratchet for the entire lift and final hold. Do not animate engagement or claim that this parked pawl holds the load. Human holding torque is required. The handle lies outside the drum journals.

Use the negative +X rotations specified for the drum and sheaves. Positive rotation would lower this routing. The short drum wrap grows from 1 to 4 radians and never forms overlapping turns. No helical wrap or hidden rope store is required.

research.identification: Ms B49r crane verified in e-Leo. Ms B49v is the separate double crane, not interchangeable [EL-CRANE].
sheet_vs_reconstruction: Sheet crane is distinguished from cannon dimensions below it [EL-CRANE]. Alcide De Rizzardi and Alessandro Siriati made IGB39 in1952 to1953 [CRANE-M]. This geometry is independent.

[folio] The sheet draws a jib on a mast with a pulley at each end, a strut from the jib down to the windlass and its toothed wheel, a box on the platform, and the platform turning over a braced base [EL-CRANE]. [geometry] The crossed sole, the running ring and its rollers, the planked platform in its felloe rim with the pin that locks it, the chamfered mast clasped between the jib's two beams, the sheaves on iron bolts, the strut and knees, the bored standards, the forged crank and ratchet, the box of stones bound with iron as the counterweight, and the lewis and ring on the dressed stone load are the museum's reconstruction of how a carpenter and a smith of about 1500 would build that [A-GEOM].
research.dimensions: No crane dimension or Richter number verified. The12braccia on49r belong to the separate weapon note, not this crane [EL-CRANE].

claims.claimed_by_leonardo: Crane purpose is inferred from drawing and model record, not a verified claim of capacity [EL-CRANE,CRANE-M].
claims.tested_by_leonardo: No dated experiment by Leonardo was verified in the sources listed here. This is an evidence gap, not proof that he never tried it.
claims.built_in_lifetime: No build by Leonardo established. Construction cranes existed in the workshops he observed [CRANE-M].
claims.later_tests: The1952 to1953 model is interpretative. No instrumented load test located [CRANE-M].

inputs: Rope centreline radius r=0.08 m, speed magnitude omega=0.25 rad/s [C,A-DETAIL]. Solid drum radius is 0.075 m and rope radius 0.005 m.
physics.limits: Illustrative balance excludes jib selfweight and anchoring. This is not a construction safety rating. The pawl is disengaged. Ideal final holding force at the hand remains 39.2 N.

myths.correction: This sheet records a particular design, not invention of the crane [CRANE-M].

research.confidence: High folio identification. ClassC geometry and capacities. Full-size structural strength unverified.
